compounds.title: completed commitment of information to retention
compounds.definition: A bounded information-retention operation completes a commitment of the relevant content of one target information item to a retained record in a contextual store. The record satisfies DAT:000 within that store at completion. Its committed content matches the target content at the operation's capture point under one fixed contextual content-equivalence criterion. ORI:110 actualizes this operation's completed retention commitment, not necessarily the target's or record's first existence. The record may be newly established or an existing record whose commitment is refreshed, including a successful unchanged-content save. No new copy, changed content, distinct source and destination contexts, physical medium, power-loss guarantee, indefinite retention, named version, later accessibility or truth of the information is implied. The target and retained record may be the same information object or distinct objects; this meaning does not decide their token identity. No external actor is supplied. Ongoing aspect views the operation internally without asserting a completed commitment.
constraints: The outer target is the information item whose relevant content is committed, not a mandatory new result token. The DAT:000 object is the retained record within one fixed contextual store.

The target's content at the capture point and the committed record satisfy one fixed contextual equivalence criterion. No exact byte, metadata, encoding or cryptographic identity follows unless that criterion includes it.
ORI:110 actualizes the completed commitment for this bounded operation. The target or record need not newly exist, and the target's content may already have been retained before the operation.

The operation may establish, refresh or affirm a matching retained record; passive pre-existing retention without this completed operation is not a commitment event. Later changes, deletion, failure and retrieval remain unspecified.
Time, negation, modality, aspect and runtime scope the entire operation, including the commitment and content relation. The contextual store and criterion must not change to manufacture success.
excludes: A target merely remains stored with no completed retention operation
A transient display, send, or in-memory calculation without a retained record result
An attempted or ongoing write reported as already committed
A distinct new copy, changed content, different storage context, permanent preservation, physical rescue or thrift inferred without being stated
compounds.example: The information-retention operation completes its commitment of the file.
compounds.near: The file was displayed, but no retained record was committed.
compounds.reuse: Reuse this exact commitment before specifying its actor, storage destination, named version, restoration or stronger durability criterion.
compounds.everyday: Completes a commitment of the item’s content to a retained record

compounds.title: caused commitment of information to retention
parts: completed commitment of information to retention
compounds.definition: An actor brings about a completed commitment of one distinct target information item's relevant content to a retained record in a contextual store. The exact information-retention commitment dependency supplies the capture point, fixed content-equivalence criterion and completed retained-record result. ORI:211 grounds that commitment in the actor's causally productive contribution, rather than mere observation, correlation or background presence. The operation may establish a record or refresh an existing commitment, including unchanged content; it does not require a distinct copy or a change to the target's relevant content. The actor may be a person, program or other operative source, without a claim of intention or consciousness. No named store, physical medium, permanent or power-loss-safe retention, subsequent access, new version, additional transfer or rescue meaning is supplied. Ongoing aspect does not assert that the saving operation has completed.
constraints: The outer actor is the operative source of the retention commitment and is distinct from its outer target information item. The actor need not be the store or be conscious.
The outer target is exactly the target of the nested commitment. Its retained record, capture point, store and equivalence criterion are the same throughout this one operation.
The ORI:211 head makes the completed commitment causally dependent on the actor's productive contribution. The retained record itself may already have existed.
A cause/target reversal changes the message. All nested commitments remain inside the event's ordered time, negation, modality, aspect and runtime scopes.
excludes: Copying requires a distinct result; saving does not
Keeping an already stored item without performing a retention commitment
Sending or showing information without committing a retained record
Rescuing a person or object, economizing money/time, physical warehousing, or asserting permanent retention
compounds.near: Nora displayed the file but never committed a retained record.
compounds.reuse: Reuse this exact saving operation before specifying a destination, named saved version, restore source or guaranteed retention duration.
compounds.everyday: Commits the item’s content to a retained information record

excluded_readings: A claim that a saving operation occurred
